summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created a worktree. It never ran `sdd-state register` or `sdd-state next`. Instead it tried to claim Task 1, found that fixture-session held it, and stopped to ask the developer which task to take. After the scripted answer "No, the other session is still working." it handed back without claiming or working Task 2, which was claimable. It never ran a --takeover command.
reasoning: Criteria 2, 3 and 5 clearly failed. The agent never ran register or next, never claimed or worked Task 2, and stopped twice on the held Task 1 to ask the developer which task to take. Criteria 1 and 4 passed: the skill was invoked and no takeover was run. The story's core intent, a second session taking the claimable task, was not met.

observations.description: The agent did not follow the held-task rule. Instead of running `sdd-state register` and `next`, it tried to claim Task 1 directly ("Now I'll try claiming Task 1, which the skill requires before anything else"). When the claim failed because the task was held, it stopped and asked the developer to pick a task. It never took Task 2, which was independent and claimable.

The skill text the agent loaded seems to support stopping. The agent quoted guidance that skipping ahead to another task "would decide it by accident" and that it should "Tell your human partner who holds the task and since when, and ask whether to take it over". This conflicts with the intended rule (take the claimable task and don't stop on the held one), so the skill wording may be the root cause.
The agent appended its session line to the shared ledger progress.md directly with `echo ... >> $W/progress.md` instead of going through an sdd-state verb such as register.

Claude Code's worktree isolation guard rejected several of the agent's compound Bash commands, including `sdd-state claim ... --session $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; echo exit=$?`. Its message was "runs sdd-state with a value computed at runtime ... Refusing to run it". The agent had to retry these as simpler commands, which added friction.

The AskUserQuestion had no option matching a plain "don't take over" answer, so I typed the scripted reply through 'Type something'. The agent then read that reply as not choosing a task and stopped completely, even though its own recommended option was 'Task 2 only'.
At startup Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt even though the launcher already passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose 'No'.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development via Skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log is `Skill: hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development`; the screen shows `⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill`.

criteria.criterion: Ran `sdd-state register` and `sdd-state next`, with `next` naming Task 2 as claimable
criteria.evidence: I ran jq on the session log to list tool_use commands and grepped for 'sdd-state (register|next|claim)'. It returned only two `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 1 --session ...` commands. There is no register and no next. The only other sdd-state verbs were `sync` and `verify`.

criteria.criterion: Claimed Task 2 with `sdd-state claim ... 2 --session ...` and worked it; the ledger has a `Task 2: branch` line
criteria.evidence: No claim command for Task 2 appears in the log; the only claims are for Task 1. progress.md contains only the fixture-session line, the plan line and the agent's own session line. There is no `Task 2:` line. The agent's final message: "I haven't claimed anything or written any code... I've stopped here."

`grep -c -- '--takeover'` on the session log found 1 match. That match is the skill text loaded into context ("take over (`--takeover`) only on their explicit yes"), not a Bash command. The jq listing of Bash commands contains no --takeover.

criteria.criterion: Did not stop at held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: After the failed claim of Task 1, the agent sent AskUserQuestion: "Task 1 (src/a.sh) is held by your other session... Which tasks should this new session work on?" The options were Task 2 only, Task 2 then Task 3, Take over Task 1, and Wait. This was a request to choose a task, not just a takeover question. After my scripted answer it handed back again: "Your answer didn't say which task this session should take instead. The workflow says to wait for your instruction rather than pick one myself, so I've stopped here."
